nodes.label: Raspberry Pi Single-Board Computer
nodes.description: Product photograph of a green Raspberry Pi board (Model B era, 2014 silkscreen, Samsung LPDDR SDRAM package, raspberry logo) on a plain light background, shot at an angle. Visible interfaces: a 40-pin GPIO header along the top-left edge, two stacked dual USB-A ports and an EDAC Ethernet RJ45 jack at the right, HDMI out and a 3.5 mm AV jack along the front, micro-USB power input, plus CSI camera and DSI display ribbon connectors and four mounting holes.
nodes.rationale: Used as the edge compute platform illustration: the 40-pin GPIO header supplies the digital I/O needed for environmental sensors and the CSI connector accepts a camera module, so a single low-cost board can host both sensing and on-device inference without a separate microcontroller.

nodes.label: 40-Pin GPIO Header
nodes.description: The general-purpose input/output pin header on the Raspberry Pi, providing 3.3 V and 5 V power rails, ground and single-wire digital data lines used to attach sensor modules.
nodes.rationale: Its VCC/GND/DATA pin availability is precisely what lets a one-wire sensor module be attached directly, with no ADC or level-shifting hardware in between.

nodes.label: Edge Compute Platform
nodes.description: Design choice of running sensing, data logging and model inference on a low-cost single-board computer deployed inside the poultry house.
nodes.rationale: On-site computation avoids dependence on continuous rural network connectivity and reduces the bandwidth and latency cost of streaming video off-farm; a general-purpose Linux SBC also allows the same device to run the detection model and read the sensors.
